subject: Physics
description: Scalar vs vector, displacement, velocity, acceleration, projectile motion

questions.stem: Which of the following is a SCALAR quantity?
questions.explanation: SCALAR — magnitude only (no direction). Examples: speed, distance, mass, time, temperature, energy, work, power, charge, density. VECTOR — magnitude + direction. Examples: displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, momentum, torque, electric/magnetic field. Speed = |velocity|; distance ≥ |displacement| (path length vs straight-line displacement). Vectors follow vector-addition (parallelogram, triangle); scalars add algebraically.

questions.stem: A car travelling at 20 m/s decelerates uniformly at 4 m/s² and comes to a stop. Distance travelled before stopping:
questions.explanation: Use v² = u² + 2as. Final v = 0, initial u = 20, a = −4 (deceleration). 0 = 400 + 2·(−4)·s → 8s = 400 → s = 50 m. Time to stop: v = u + at → 0 = 20 + (−4)t → t = 5 s. Or use s = ut + ½at² = 20(5) + ½(−4)(25) = 100 − 50 = 50 m ✓.

questions.stem: An object is in projectile motion. At the highest point of the trajectory, its:

options.option_text: Velocity is zero in both x and y
Vertical (y) velocity is zero, but horizontal (x) velocity remains constant

questions.explanation: Projectile motion = independent x + y. x-component: a_x = 0 (no horizontal force, ignoring air drag) → v_x = u·cosθ constant throughout. y-component: a_y = −g (downward) → v_y = u·sinθ − gt. At highest point, v_y = 0 (rising stops) → t = u·sinθ/g; H_max = (u·sinθ)²/(2g); Range R = u²·sin(2θ)/g. Maximum range at θ = 45°. Acceleration is g (downward) at all times — never zero. Total speed at top = u·cosθ (horizontal only).

questions.stem: If two forces of 3 N and 4 N act on a body at right angles, the magnitude of the resultant is:
questions.explanation: For two perpendicular vectors: |R|² = |A|² + |B|² → |R| = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 N. Direction tan θ = 4/3 → θ ≈ 53° from the 3-N vector. For non-perpendicular: |R|² = |A|² + |B|² + 2|A||B|·cosα, where α is the angle between them. Max R = A + B when α = 0; min R = |A − B| when α = 180°. For 3 + 4 vectors, range is 1 N to 7 N.

questions.stem: A body moves around a circle of radius r at constant speed v. Its acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Even at constant SPEED, the velocity vector changes direction continuously → acceleration is non-zero. Centripetal acceleration a_c = v²/r, always pointing towards the centre. Force F = m·v²/r is the net inward force (provided by gravity for satellites; tension for a stone on a string; normal/friction for a car on a curved road). Without this force, body would move tangentially (Newton's 1st law). Centrifugal 'force' is a pseudo-force in rotating frame — not a real force.

questions.stem: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with initial velocity 20 m/s (g = 10 m/s²). Time to reach maximum height:
questions.explanation: At maximum height, v = 0. Use v = u − gt (taking up positive, g acts down): 0 = 20 − 10t → t = 2 s. Maximum height: h = u·t − ½g·t² = 20·2 − ½·10·4 = 40 − 20 = 20 m. Total time of flight (up and back down) = 4 s. By symmetry, time up = time down = 2 s; the ball returns with same speed (20 m/s, but downward).

questions.stem: A man walks 4 km East then 3 km North. His total DISPLACEMENT (straight-line distance from start) is:
questions.explanation: DISTANCE traversed = 4 + 3 = 7 km (scalar, path length). DISPLACEMENT = vector from start to end = √(4² + 3²) = 5 km in direction NE (tan⁻¹(3/4) ≈ 37° North of East). Distance ≥ |displacement| always. Equal only when motion is in a single direction. The 3-4-5 right-triangle is the most familiar Pythagorean triple — useful pattern to recognise instantly.
